title: Acceptance-Controlled MIS-PO: Adaptive Trajectory Filtering for Stable Off-Policy RLVR Training

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The purpose of the contribution is to identify what drives stability in off-policy RLVR trajectory filtering under high staleness. None of the prior papers explicitly investigates this specific empirical relationship or reports findings about the drivers of stability in trajectory filtering under high staleness. While several papers address stability in off-policy RL (e.g., [1], [5], [9]), they focus on different aspects such as variance reduction, safety guarantees, or Lyapunov stability, rather than isolating the role of trajectory filtering bound magnitudes. No prior work establishes the same empirical relationship.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves ablation of trajectory filtering bound magnitudes in MIS-PO, isolating bound tightness from adaptive control. Paper [5] discusses trajectory filtering in the context of off-policy RL for LLMs, specifically addressing variance reduction and stability through sequence-level normalization and clipping. However, it does not isolate bound tightness as a driver of stability, nor does it perform ablations specific to bound magnitudes. Paper [18] also discusses importance sampling ratios and their impact on stability but does not focus on trajectory filtering bounds. No prior paper implements the exact mechanism of isolating bound tightness through ablation in MIS-PO.

### Evaluation
The evaluation design involves measuring the impact of tighter trajectory bounds on stability and performance, yielding a +12.76 percentage point improvement over default MIS-PO bounds. Paper [5] evaluates stability improvements in off-policy RL for LLMs using sequence-level clipping and normalization, which is a substantively equivalent evaluation design. Both contributions assess stability improvements in off-policy RL pipelines by modifying trajectory filtering mechanisms and measuring performance gains. The specific benchmark or metric instance differs, but the evaluation design is covered.

### Domain
The domain is off-policy RLVR training of LLMs. Paper [5] explicitly addresses off-policy RL for LLMs, focusing on variance reduction and stability in this domain. Paper [18] also operates in the same domain, discussing importance sampling and stability in off-policy RL for LLMs. Thus, the domain is covered.

## Purpose: Remove manual tuning of trajectory filtering bounds across staleness levels and training stages.

The purpose is to eliminate manual hyperparameter tuning of filtering/clipping bounds in off-policy LLM training. Paper [4] (BAPO) addresses stabilizing off-policy RL for LLMs with adaptive clipping, but its purpose is stabilization/alignment, not specifically eliminating manual tuning of filtering bounds. Paper [9] (AdaGC) aims to eliminate manual gradient clipping threshold selection — "requires hand selection of a clipping threshold hyperparameter" — but for pretraining, not trajectory filtering. Paper [14] (AutoClip) explicitly targets "automatically and adaptively choosing a gradient clipping threshold" to remove hand-selection. Paper [8] (TF-ASMC) proposes to "eliminate the need of design for switching threshold and inherent threshold-tuning." These are about gradient clipping thresholds, not trajectory filtering bounds in off-policy RLVR. However, the underlying objective — remove manual tuning of a bound/threshold parameter — is shared at the problem-class level. Paper [14] most directly covers this: eliminating manual selection of a clipping bound by making it adaptive. The domain differs (audio source separation vs. LLM RLVR), but the purpose at the problem-class level is the same.

## Mechanism: Adaptive controller targeting a pre-specified acceptance rate schedule using quantile estimation with EMA smoothing to set bound magnitudes automatically.

The mechanism combines: (1) targeting a pre-specified acceptance rate (like a PI/proportional controller targeting a setpoint), (2) quantile estimation to set thresholds, (3) EMA smoothing. Paper [14] (AutoClip) uses "history of gradient norms observed during training" with percentile (quantile) estimation to set clipping thresholds adaptively — this is quantile-based adaptive threshold setting. Paper [9] (AdaGC) uses adaptive gradient clipping with EMA-based statistics. Paper [12] (AGP for WGANs) uses a PI controller to adjust a penalty coefficient based on real-time training feedback targeting a setpoint — "employs a Proportional–Integral (PI) controller to adjust the gradient penalty coefficient λt based on real-time training feedback." This is a controller targeting a pre-specified rate/value using feedback. The combination of quantile estimation + EMA + acceptance-rate targeting as a unified controller is not fully present in any single paper. Paper [14] covers quantile-based adaptive clipping. Paper [12] covers PI-controller-based adaptive penalty targeting a setpoint. No single paper combines all three elements (acceptance rate schedule + quantile estimation + EMA) for trajectory filtering bounds. The closest is [14] for quantile-based adaptive threshold, but the acceptance-rate-schedule targeting with EMA is not present there.

## Evaluation: Controller discovers bound magnitudes automatically while maintaining stable training under staleness s=256, where Fixed MIS-PO crashed.

The evaluation design is a stability comparison between adaptive and fixed configurations under high staleness, measuring training stability (crash vs. no crash). This is a substitution/ablation experiment comparing adaptive vs. fixed hyperparameters on a training stability metric. Papers [4], [1], [13], [18] all evaluate off-policy LLM training stability with comparisons between methods. Paper [4] specifically compares adaptive clipping vs. fixed approaches in off-policy LLM settings. The evaluation design (compare adaptive vs. fixed bound under stress conditions, measure stability) is a standard ablation/comparison design used in [4], [9], [14]. However, the specific design of testing under a named staleness level (s=256) as a stress test is specific to this work. The generic design of "adaptive vs. fixed, measure stability" is covered by [4] and [14].

## Domain: Off-policy RLVR training of LLMs.

Papers [1], [4], [10], [13], [18] all work in off-policy RL training of LLMs. This domain is clearly covered.
